transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-01
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Jordan Patel (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (CTO - Astrolabe), Priya Singh (ML Eng), Evan Reyes (DevOps), Sofia Martins (Head InfoSec)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
Astrolabe is evaluating Redwood's hosted API for a PLG onramp but has strong constraints around EU data residency and keys; exploring Dedicated and Private for low-latency inference in EU region. Main asks: time-to-first-token, free credits for pilot, benchmark numbers, SOC2/KMS details, and cost per 1k tokens at the expected QPS. Action: Redwood to run perf test, share pricing doc, schedule security deep-dive.

Topics:
- Quickstart & time-to-first-token
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
- Security/compliance (SOC2, KMS, audit logs, VPC)
- Cost/latency goals and batching recommendations
- Pilot/POC scope and success criteria

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, can you hear me okay?
[00:03] Liam (Astrolabe): Yep, loud and clear. Thanks for setting this up, Maya.
[00:06] Maya: Cool. Quick intros, I'm Maya, I'm the AE working with platform teams, Jordan is our solutions engineer who will cover perf and infra details.
[00:11] Jordan (Redwood SE): Hey all.
[00:12] Priya: Priya, ML eng, I own the models and prompt infra.
[00:14] Evan: Evan, platform eng, I handle our CI/CD and k8s infra.
[00:17] Sofia: Sofia, head of InfoSec, I'll be driving the security checklist.
[00:19] Maya: Awesome. The goal today is to understand your constraints — especially around residency, latency, and pilot timeline — and then map which Redwood delivery option makes sense: hosted API quickstart vs Dedicated reserved capacity vs Private deployment.
[00:28] Liam: Briefly, Astrolabe is building a routing/ETA product for logistics. We have EU customers and some internal PII, so residency matters. We're in early PLG phase, want a low-friction dev experience to ship a proof of value to product teams within 2–3 weeks. But if it hits production, we need predictable throughput and compliance.
[00:44] Maya: Makes sense. When you say low-friction, do you mean zero infra on your side — i.e., use Redwood hosted endpoints to move fast?
[00:48] Priya: Ideally yes, devs want keys and an SDK. But security will push back unless we can show audit logs and encryption in transit and at rest. Also, time-to-first-token is key — we can't wait a week to onboard.
[00:58] Sofia: Right, plus a KMS integration for customer-encrypted data would be ideal. We prefer Bring Your Own Key for any PII fields.
[01:03] Jordan: Okay, good to know. For hosted we have region controls and EU zones; we also support customer-managed keys in some Private offerings. There're tradeoffs — hosted is fastest to start (minutes to token), Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and predictable p99 latency, and Private (VPC or on-prem) gets you complete control for compliance.
[01:20] Evan: Can you quantify "minutes to token"? Our devs want a sandbox they can hit today.
[01:24] Maya: For self-serve hosted: sign up, get API key, SDK quickstart, you'll hit first token in under 30 minutes normally — including demo prompts. With our free credits we can seed a POC for a couple thousand requests so devs can iterate.
[01:34] Priya: Free credits — is there a standard amount? We want to test at 100–200 QPS peaks for a day.
[01:39] Maya: We usually allocate pilot credits tailored to the use case; I'll propose an allocation enough for ~50k generated tokens and a short perf run. For sustained 100–200 QPS you'd quickly exceed pilot credits, but we can run a benchmark on our side to simulate that.
[01:51] Liam: If initial tests look good, what's the path to Dedicated? Time to provision?
[01:55] Jordan: Dedicated pools are typically a few days after contract — depends on capacity and region. For EU we can often provision within 3–7 business days if there's immediate capacity. Private on-prem takes more planning — packaging, network setup, and security review can be 4–8 weeks.
[02:07] Sofia: For Private we'd need to know about HSM/KMS integration, audit logs export to our SIEM, and support for our SCAP baseline.
[02:13] Jordan: We have connectors for common KMS providers and we can ship audit logs to S3/GCS or directly to your SIEM via secure forwarding. The SCAP baseline we can map in the security deep-dive.
[02:21] Evan: What about model control — can we pin model versions? We want deterministic outputs for regressions.
[02:25] Jordan: Yes, model pinning and rollouts are supported. We also have model variants for quantized inference to trade off cost vs quality.
[02:31] Priya: How accurate are your latency numbers? Our users expect sub-200ms p50 for short prompts (<=128 tokens).
[02:36] Jordan: On dedicated GPU pools with optimized kernels and batching tuned, p50 sub-200ms is achievable for small prompts. Hosted can hit sub-300ms typical but depends on load and region affinity. P99s will be higher; we can surface token-level latency breakdowns in the console.
[02:49] Liam: Is there an SLA for p99 latency or only uptime?
[02:52] Maya: Our SLA currently focuses on availability for hosted and Dedicated tiers. Latency SLOs are documented per model and Dedicated contract can include tighter SLOs. We do rollback and fallback routing to keep applications online if a model variant misbehaves.
[03:05] Sofia: Security question — where are keys stored? Are they ever accessible to Redwood employees?
[03:09] Jordan: KMS-managed keys are customer-controlled in Private. For hosted we store encrypted keys; access is tightly controlled and audited. We can provide SOC2 reports and an access matrix in the security folder.
[03:19] Priya: When you say "fallback routing" — is that transparent to the app or do we need to handle errors?
[03:23] Jordan: That's configurable. We can do automatic fallback to a lower-cost model variant or another region. The system will return a warning header you can log; you can also request hard failures if you prefer strict consistency.
[03:34] Evan: For our CI/CD, we want a staging endpoint that mirrors production traffic. Can we have a dedicated route per environment?
[03:38] Maya: Yes, you can create separate API keys and per-route dashboards. Billing and cost attribution are token-level, so staging and prod can be split out.
[03:46] Liam: Cost — give me a ballpark for per-1k token cost hosted vs Dedicated.
[03:50] Maya: Ballpark: hosted with standard open models is lowest friction but per-token cost is higher than Dedicated per-unit once committed. Dedicated pricing involves reserved instance commitments; unit cost can drop 30–60% depending on scale. I'll put exact numbers in the pricing worksheet I send.
[04:03] Priya: We need a bench to validate hallucination rates too. Do you support evals and comparison tooling?
[04:07] Jordan: Yes, Redwood Optimize has eval suites, regression alerts, and prompt-set tied monitoring. We can run an automated eval across prompt sets to measure quality drift.
[04:15] Sophia (sic) [transcription error for Sofia]: Sorry, did you say Redwood Optimize? Is that included or an add-on?
[04:19] Maya: It's an add-on but often bundled for pilots with enterprise engagements.
[04:22] Priya: On the pilot scope — what success metrics should we define? For us maybe: sub-200ms p50 on key prompts, <2% unacceptable hallucinations on the QA set, and cost per request under X.
[04:35] Liam: Also, we want <500ms tail on average for our user flows.
[04:39] Jordan: We'll capture p50/p95/p99 in the perf run. For hallucination rates we'll run an eval against your sample prompts — Priya can share those.
[04:47] Priya: I'll share a small set of 200 prompts and expected answers; probably by Thursday.
[04:51] Maya: Great. A few more practical items: onboarding for hosted is self-serve; for Dedicated we do a short planning call and some infra-level config. Billing-wise, hosted is usage-based; Dedicated is monthly commit. Private is licensed + integration.
[05:04] Evan: For Dedicated, is there an option for burst capacity if we have traffic spikes?
[05:08] Jordan: Yes, we offer burst capacity and autoscaling policies; Dedicated can be configured to allow controlled burst to shared pools, with cost controls.
[05:17] Liam: Any gotchas around VPC peering or network egress? For EU we must avoid cross-border egress and need NAT control.
[05:23] Jordan: For Private we can deploy in your VPC. For Dedicated we support VPC peering/PrivateLink in major clouds; we can also provide egress controls and whitelist IPs. We'll need your network team involved for peering.
[05:33] Sofia: On logging, we need immutable audit logs for admin actions and model access. Can logs be forwarded to our SIEM and kept for a year?
[05:39] Jordan: Yes, logs can be forwarded and retention is configurable; for enterprise customers we support 1+ year. We'll add details in the security doc.
[05:47] Priya: Slight concern — some model names keep changing in OSS; how much control do we have over model upgrades?
[05:51] Jordan: You can pin versions, opt-in to auto-upgrades, or test new versions in a canary rollout. We also maintain performance profiles per model to help you choose.
[05:59] Liam: If we start with hosted plus credits, and we'd like to add Dedicated later, how seamless is the switch?
[06:03] Maya: It's designed to be smooth — same API, same SDKs and tooling. You'll change the endpoint or the routing policy; pinners and keys can be re-used or rotated as needed.
[06:11] Evan: Do you provide client libraries with typed responses? We rely on structured output for our post-processing.
[06:15] Jordan: SDKs support streaming, tool-calling patterns, and structured JSON outputs. We have SDKs for Node, Python, and Go.
[06:21] Priya: One more — do you have examples for batching and KV cache patterns to reduce token costs?
[06:25] Jordan: Yep, we have guides and auto-batching recommendations in Redwood Optimize; runtime handles KV cache for multi-turn chat to save tokens. We'll share the batching guide.
[06:33] Maya: Ok quick pause — any blockers for running a hosted perf run?
[06:36] Priya: We'll need the endpoint and maybe some sample data; otherwise no blocker.
[06:40] Jordan: I'll run a perf test on our side with a synthetic workload similar to your target QPS and both short and long sequences.
[06:46] Liam: On pilot timeline — we want the POC to show to product teams within 2 weeks, ideally with perf and early UX. Does that sound feasible?
[06:53] Maya: Absolutely for a hosted pilot. Dedicated would take longer but we can do a hosted-to-dedicated path if results look good.
[06:58] Sofia: We'll review the SOC2 artifacts and ask follow-ups. If compliance checks out, Private might be attractive for long-term.
[07:04] Maya: Noted. We'll share SOC2 and a proposed checklist itemizing what we can provide.
[07:09] Evan: Any references or case studies for EU-based customers?
[07:12] Maya: I'll include a short case study of a European retailer we onboarded to Dedicated with VPC peering and KMS BYOK.
[07:18] Priya: Okay, let's map owners — Priya will send prompt set, Sofia will send security requirements, Maya will send pricing and deck, Jordan will run perf.
[07:26] Maya: Cool. Are there any other questions or concerns?
[07:29] Liam: Only one more — do you support live streaming of tokens to clients for progressive rendering?
[07:33] Jordan: Yes, streaming is supported by the hosted API; we also provide hooks for function/tool calling.
[07:38] Priya: Great.
[07:39] Maya: Alright, we'll follow up with the materials. Thanks everyone.
[07:42] [Crosstalk/overlap] Liam: Thanks, bye.
[07:44] End of call.
